auth.description: Statuspage API key, sent as the Authorization header after the literal scheme word `OAuth ` — a static key from the account's own API settings, not an OAuth2 access token
auth.name: statuspage.api_key
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: The id of the status page this connection administers. Statuspage shows it in the address bar of the page's own management screen (manage.statuspage.io/pages/<page id>) and on the API keys screen. One connection administers one page: an account with several status pages needs one installation per page
config.label: Status page id
config.name: page_id

config.help: Create one under your Statuspage user account's API keys screen. The key carries the permissions of the account that created it, so an account that should only read incidents must not be the one that mints this key. Statuspage shows the key once
config.label: Statuspage API key
config.name: api_key

description: Atlassian Statuspage: read a status page's components and incidents, and open or update a publicly visible incident on it

operations.description: List this status page's incidents, most recent first — both unresolved and already-resolved ones. Returns Statuspage's own first page of results; this connector declares no paging parameters, so a page with a long incident history is not enumerated exhaustively here

response_schema.description: The page's incidents, most recent first. Statuspage returns a bare JSON array here, not an object wrapping one

components.description: The components this incident affects, in the shape statuspage-component-list returns

id.description: The incident's own id — what statuspage-incident-get and statuspage-incident-update address it by

impact.description: none, maintenance, minor, major or critical — Statuspage's own calculation from the affected components unless an override was set

incident_updates.description: Every update posted to this incident, most recent first. Each update's body is what subscribers received

body.description: The publicly visible message this update posted

monitoring_at.description: When the incident moved to monitoring; null until it does

name.description: The incident's title, as shown on the public page

page_id.description: The page this incident belongs to — the same id this connection is configured with

resolved_at.description: When the incident was resolved; null until it is

shortlink.description: The public short URL for this incident

status.description: investigating, identified, monitoring or resolved for a realtime incident; scheduled, in_progress, verifying or completed for a scheduled maintenance, which this connector does not create or update

operations.description: Get one incident on this status page, including every update posted to it so far

params.description: The incident's own id, from statuspage-incident-list's `id` field or from statuspage-incident-create's response
params.name: incident_id

impact.description: none, maintenance, minor, major or critical

incident_updates.description: Every update posted to this incident, most recent first. Each update's body is what subscribers received

body.description: The publicly visible message this update posted

name.description: The incident's title, as shown on the public page

shortlink.description: The public short URL for this incident

status.description: investigating, identified, monitoring or resolved for a realtime incident

operations.description: Open a new incident on this status page. It is public the moment this call returns — anyone loading the page sees it, and with deliver_notifications true Statuspage emails and texts every subscriber the page has. The incident itself is reversible (resolve it, or delete it), but a notification that has been sent cannot be recalled, so treat deliver_notifications as the irreversible half of this call

params.description: The incident's title, shown on the public status page and used as the subject line of the notification. Write it for the page's readers, not for an operator
params.name: name

params.description: The lifecycle stage this incident opens in. investigating means the cause is not yet known; identified means it is; monitoring means a fix is deployed and being watched; resolved opens the incident already closed, which is how a retroactive record of a past outage is posted
params.name: status

params.description: The first update's message, shown publicly under the incident and sent verbatim to subscribers if deliver_notifications is true. This is the text the outside world reads, so it must not contain internal hostnames, customer identifiers or anything else not meant to leave the organisation
params.name: body

params.description: Whether to notify subscribers. true emails and texts every subscriber this page has, immediately and irreversibly; false publishes the incident to the page silently. There is no default here on purpose — publishing to a public page is a choice about an audience, and this connector requires it to be made explicitly on every call
params.name: deliver_notifications

id.description: The new incident's id — what statuspage-incident-get and statuspage-incident-update address it by

impact.description: Statuspage's own calculation for the new incident

incident_updates.description: The one update this call posted

shortlink.description: The public short URL for this incident — already live

operations.description: Post an update to an existing incident on this status page, moving it to a new lifecycle stage and adding a publicly visible message. The update appears on the page immediately, and with deliver_notifications true Statuspage emails and texts every subscriber. The incident's status can be moved again afterwards, but a notification that has been sent cannot be recalled. Does not rename the incident — this operation cannot change its title

params.description: The incident's own id, from statuspage-incident-list's `id` field or statuspage-incident-create's response
params.name: incident_id

params.description: The lifecycle stage to move the incident to. resolved closes it and marks the status page green again if nothing else is open; monitoring says a fix is deployed and being watched; identified says the cause is known. Moving to a stage the incident is already in is allowed and simply posts another update
params.name: status

params.description: This update's message, shown publicly under the incident and sent verbatim to subscribers if deliver_notifications is true. Required by this connector rather than by Statuspage: an update with no message posts an empty entry to a page the outside world reads
params.name: body

params.description: Whether to notify subscribers of this update. true emails and texts every subscriber immediately and irreversibly; false posts the update to the page silently. Required on every call for the same reason as on statuspage-incident-create — the audience is a choice, not a default
params.name: deliver_notifications

incident_updates.description: Every update on the incident including the one this call just posted, most recent first

name.description: Unchanged — this operation cannot rename an incident

resolved_at.description: Set once the status reaches resolved

operations.description: List the components this status page publishes — the individual services whose operational state the page shows. Takes no parameter at all and succeeds for any page the API key can administer, which is what makes it the connection check for a settings page's Test Connection button. Returns Statuspage's own first page of results; this connector declares no paging parameters

response_schema.description: The page's components, in the page's own display order. Statuspage returns a bare JSON array here, not an object wrapping one

description.description: The component's own description, shown on the public page

group.description: Whether this entry is a component *group* rather than a component

group_id.description: The id of the group this component belongs to; null when it is ungrouped or is itself a group

name.description: The component's name as shown on the public page

only_show_if_degraded.description: Whether the component is hidden from the public page while it is operational

position.description: Display order within the page or the component group

showcase.description: Whether the component is shown on the public page at all

start_date.description: The date this component's uptime history begins, as YYYY-MM-DD

status.description: operational, under_maintenance, degraded_performance, partial_outage or major_outage
